### Reading Comprehension — Questions 96–100

Read the passage carefully.

Restoring a mangrove forest is not simply a matter of planting seedlings along a coastline. Successful restoration depends on understanding tidal movement, soil salinity, sediment supply and the species naturally suited to each site. Projects that disregard these conditions may show rapid initial growth but fail as seedlings are washed away or cannot tolerate the prevailing salinity. In some locations, removing barriers to natural water flow can allow mangroves to regenerate without extensive planting. This is why restoration programmes increasingly combine ecological surveys with community participation and long-term monitoring.
